notes: STACK staking: Solidity ^0.8.30, Foundry project (solc 0.8.30, optimizer profile 1M runs via_ir for other contracts; Staking.sol itself compiled under default profile). Deps: OpenZeppelin Ownable, IERC20, SafeERC20, SafeCast only. No proxies, no upgradeability, single Ownable admin (expected to be Safe DAO).

STACK staking trust boundaries: stake/initiateWithdrawal*/claimWithdrawal are permissionless and move SAFE tokens; proposeValidators/proposeWithdrawDelay/recoverTokens are onlyOwner; executeWithdrawDelayChange/executeValidatorChanges are PUBLIC but bound by timelock + stored hash/proposal. SAFE_TOKEN is an immutable deploy-time choice; standard ERC20 assumed (no fee-on-transfer handling).

STACK staking state: stakes[staker][validator], totalValidatorStakes, totalStakerStakes, totalStakedAmount, totalPendingWithdrawals accounting counters; per-staker doubly linked withdrawal queues (withdrawalQueues + withdrawalNodes) keyed by globally unique uint64 IDs from nextWithdrawalId (starts at 1); pendingWithdrawDelayChange (ConfigProposal) and pendingValidatorChangeHash (bytes32) hold timelocked proposals.

STACK staking queue invariants (verified by reading): insertion keeps claimableAt sorted; initiateWithdrawal traverses backwards from tail; initiateWithdrawalAtPosition takes caller-supplied previousId but indexes withdrawalNodes[msg.sender] only and rejects empty nodes (claimableAt==0) and ordering violations; claimWithdrawal claims head only and requires block.timestamp >= claimableAt; H-01's cross-queue attack shape is structurally impossible because node IDs are globally unique and the mapping is per-staker (see exclusion list — do not re-report).

STACK staking error boundaries: all state mutations precede external token calls (CEI); recoverTokens computes SAFE excess as balance - totalStakedAmount - totalPendingWithdrawals with checked math (reverts on underflow); claimableAt is computed as uint128(block.timestamp + withdrawDelay) with an UNCHECKED cast while proposeWithdrawDelay uses SafeCast toUint128 for executableAt — asymmetry noted for Hunter attention, not a finding.

STACK recovery: Solidity >=0.8.12 <0.9.0, Hardhat project, OZ 4.9.x (SignatureChecker), safe-contracts 1.4.1. Module is a singleton deployed once and enabled per-Safe; all wallet state keyed by wallet address in shared mappings.

STACK recovery trust boundaries: guardian management (add/revoke/changeThreshold) is gated by onlyWhenModuleIsEnabled — caller must be a Safe with THIS module enabled, and state is keyed by msg.sender (the Safe). Recovery confirmation is guardian-signed EIP-712 (domain: NAME/VERSION/chainId/this) verified via SignatureChecker (EOA + ERC-1271). finalizeRecovery is callable by ANYONE once the timelock passes and drives owner replacement via execTransactionFromModule. cancelRecovery/invalidateNonce are keyed by msg.sender (only meaningful when the Safe itself calls).

STACK recovery state: GuardianStorageEntry per wallet (sentinel-linked guardian list + count + threshold); recoveryRequests per wallet (approval count, newThreshold, executeAfter, newOwners); confirmedHashes[recoveryHash][guardian]; walletsNonces per wallet (incremented on _executeRecovery and invalidateNonce).

STACK recovery lifecycle: confirmations accumulate per (wallet, newOwners, newThreshold, nonce) hash; execution requires current-guardian approvals >= current threshold; an ongoing request can be REPLACED only by strictly more approvals; finalize after recoveryPeriod removes all old owners except the first (tail-to-head removal loop with threshold 1), swaps/adds new owners (threshold 1), then sets newThreshold if > 1; new owners must not be current guardians (checked at finalize time, not at confirmation time).

STACK recovery formal verification: certora specs cover guardian add/revoke invariants, confirmRecovery initiation rules, cancel/finalize behavior, and nonce invalidation (rule list in LEDGER context; Hunter must read the .spec files for exact properties). Verified properties that hold are exclusions by root cause.

UNRESOLVED boundaries: (1) deployed bytecode equivalence to the pinned tags was NOT verified (no on-chain check in this run; deployments repo not consulted) — findings are source-level; (2) OZ version in safenet lib submodules not resolved (submodules empty; POC setup must init them and record versions); (3) Safe core behavior (OwnerManager/ModuleManager semantics) taken from the 1.4.1 interfaces as evidence — Hunters must verify call-level assumptions (e.g. removeOwner/addOwnerWithThreshold revert conditions) against safe-contracts 1.4.1 source, not assume them.
